links.title: Introduction
links.summary: Learn what the interactive documentation prototype demonstrates and how its playground, navigation, and examples fit together.

links.title: Overview
links.summary: Review the prototype's main surfaces: the documentation rail, executable code editor, language controls, and guarded server proxy.

links.title: Key concepts
links.summary: Understand the core ideas represented here, including model requests, structured messages, server-side execution, and safe defaults.

links.title: Next steps
links.summary: Use the prototype as a starting point for deeper documentation, production authentication, distributed limits, and provider observability.

links.title: Quickstart
links.summary: Follow the shortest path through the sample: inspect the request, choose a language view, and run only against an explicitly enabled server.

links.title: Libraries
links.summary: See where client libraries belong in the request flow and why credentials and provider calls stay behind the server boundary.

links.title: Models
links.summary: Explore how the sample selects an allowed model and how deployments can narrow, but never silently expand, the checked-in allow-list.

links.title: Deprecations
links.summary: Plan for evolving model and API surfaces by keeping examples version-aware, validated, and explicit about unsupported behavior.

links.title: Tutorials
links.summary: Build guided learning flows around the playground while preserving the same validation, authorization, and spend-control boundaries.

links.title: Policies
links.summary: Connect implementation choices to usage policies, data handling expectations, and the deployment controls required beyond this prototype.

links.title: GPT
links.summary: Use the editor request as a compact example of sending structured messages to a text model through a controlled server route.

links.title: GPT best practices
links.summary: Keep prompts focused, validate request shape, constrain accepted models, and surface failures without exposing provider credentials.

links.title: Image generation
links.summary: Treat image generation as a separate capability requiring its own request schema, output handling, policy checks, and user feedback.

links.title: Fine-tuning
links.summary: Frame fine-tuning as a managed workflow with curated data, evaluation criteria, versioned artifacts, and explicit deployment decisions.

links.title: Embeddings
links.summary: Use embeddings for similarity and retrieval workflows while defining input limits, storage boundaries, and evaluation up front.

links.title: Speech to text
links.summary: Design transcription flows around explicit media handling, supported formats, bounded uploads, and clear processing states.

links.title: Moderation
links.summary: Place moderation within a broader safety workflow that defines what is checked, how decisions are handled, and when humans intervene.

links.title: Rate limits
links.summary: Handle capacity explicitly with bounded retries and backoff; the prototype's process-local budget is not a distributed production limiter.

links.title: Error codes
links.summary: Translate validation, authorization, provider, timeout, and capacity failures into stable responses without leaking sensitive details.

links.title: Safety best practices
links.summary: Layer request validation, authentication, policy enforcement, monitoring, and human review according to the application's risk.

links.title: Production best practices
links.summary: Replace prototype controls with durable identity, distributed rate limits, observability, secret management, and tested failure recovery.

links.title: Introduction
links.summary: Understand plugin-style integrations as external capabilities with explicit schemas, trust boundaries, and user-visible actions.

links.title: Getting started
links.summary: Begin with one narrowly scoped capability, a clear contract, predictable errors, and a local test path before connecting live services.

links.title: Authentication
links.summary: Keep integration credentials server-side and choose an authentication model that makes user identity and delegated access explicit.

links.title: Examples
links.summary: Use examples to demonstrate complete request and response contracts, including validation failures and safe handling of external data.

links.title: Production
links.summary: Harden integrations with availability controls, auditability, revocable credentials, schema compatibility, and monitored dependencies.

links.title: Plugin review
links.summary: Review declared capabilities, data access, authentication, failure modes, and user consent before treating an integration as ready.

links.title: Plugin policies
links.summary: Document acceptable behavior and data use for integrations, then enforce those rules through product controls and operational review.
